title: Role succession mini-sprint and delegation checklist
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a compact 90-day mini-sprint for role succession or internal promotion with a paired hiring/backfill contingency. Goal: preserve service continuity, reduce time-to-impact for the incoming owner, and create a repeatable delegation and knowledge-transfer pattern that People Ops and Hiring Managers can reuse.

Scope:
- Target roles: IC-3 to IC-5 and first-level manager handoffs where uninterrupted project delivery is critical.
- When to run: triggered by an announced internal move, extended leave, or anticipated departure (>6 weeks notice).
- Outputs: handoff ledger, candidate hiring plan (if backfill), interview rubric, 30/60/90 onboarding checklist, mentoring rota, risk register.

High-level timeline (mini-sprint):
- Week 0 (plan & announce): create handoff ledger, confirm scope with manager, decide internal vs external backfill, schedule shadowing blocks.
- Week 1-2 (intensive transfer): run daily 30-60m knowledge sessions, pair-programing, doc cleanup.
- Week 3-4 (ride-along): incoming owner begins taking ownership for low-risk work with mentor close by.
- Month 2 (scale ownership): incoming leads sprints, takes primary on 1–2 features, weekly sync reduces to biweekly coaching.
- Month 3 (stabilize): owner fully owns routing, escalation, and backlog; handoff retrospective + retention packet.

Success metrics (fit-for-purpose):
- Operational: less than 2 critical incidents attributable to knowledge gaps in first 90 days.
- Delivery: incoming owner delivers first sprint goals by end of month 2.
- People: at least 80% confidence rating from stakeholders on owner readiness in retrospective survey.

Hiring plan decision matrix (internal move preferred when):
- High domain knowledge required and internal candidate exists with >=6 months exposure.
- Low ramp cost relative to external hire (measured by required training weeks).
- Team capacity to run a mentorship rota.
If external hire required: run condensed 4-week recruitment sprint in parallel with knowledge transfer to minimize vacancy time.

Interview rubric (for external backfill or promotion calibration):
Scoring: 1 = no evidence, 3 = meets expectations, 5 = exceeds expectations. Use whole-number scores.
- Role competency (technical): architecture understanding, debugging depth, code review quality.
- Product judgment: prioritization rationale, feature tradeoffs, stakeholder communication.
- Execution & ownership: delivery record, follow-through, incident postmortems.
- Collaboration & mentorship: cross-team communication, async docs, feedback loops.
- Culture fit & escalation style: psychological safety, escalation thresholds.
Suggested pass threshold: total >= 18/25 for senior IC; for manager roles add management rubric; require at least 2 interviewers with >=4 on execution.
Example behavioral probes:
- "Describe a time you owned an on-call incident end-to-end. What did you document afterwards?"
- "Walk me through a decision where you deprioritized a feature—what signals did you use?"
- "How do you transfer knowledge to someone unfamiliar with the codebase in 48 hours?"
Scoring notes: encourage interviewers to provide a 1-2 sentence justification for any score <=2 or >=5.

30/60/90 onboarding checklist (for incoming owner) - condensed
- Day 0–7: account access validated, infra passwords, runbooks bookmarked, 1:1 set with manager and mentor, shadow 2 triage sessions, read backlog and outstanding PRs.
- Week 2–4: take lead on one low-risk task, document 3 operational gaps, own weekly stand, run first retrospective with mentor present.
- Month 2: primary on 2 features, contribute to roadmap planning, lead cross-team sync.
- Month 3: owner of routing/triage, conduct a knowledge-share session with at least 3 stakeholders, participate in SLA review.

Knowledge-transfer ledger (handbook template lines to fill):
- Critical services & owners
- Recent incidents & postmortems (links)
- Daily/weekly operational cadence
- High-priority backlog items + blockers
- Runbook links and failover steps
- Key contacts (infra, security, product)
- Known technical debt and mitigation plan
(This doc should be a living set of short bullet points — not a long narrative.)

Mentor pairing & meeting cadence:
- Primary mentor assigned for 6–12 weeks. Weekly 1:1 first month, then biweekly.
- Secondary mentor: domain-specific (security, infra) available for ad-hoc calls.
- Shadow schedule: 4–8 paired sessions in first 2 weeks (debugging, deploy, incident triage).

Risk register (starter list):
- Knowledge gaps in incident runbooks — mitigation: pair triage and runbook rewrite within week 2.
- Single-owner service risk — mitigation: identify backup and scheduled cross-training.
- Hiring timeline slip — mitigation: short-term contractor + re-prioritize non-critical items.

Communication & stakeholder playbook:
- Announcement template: role move, interim contacts, expectations for 30/60/90, link to handoff ledger.
- Weekly status update until stabilization (first 90 days).
- Post-handoff retrospective shared with People Ops and Engineering leadership.

Quick artifacts to create in parallel:
- Handoff ledger (Google doc link)
- New-owner onboarding checklist (this doc summarized into a checklist)
- Interview scorecard (Google Form) for any external candidate
- Mentor rota calendar invite template

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes-to-self style):
- Decide whether to require a formal SLT sign-off for manager-level successions.
- Template for contractor contingency (hours, NDA, ramp expectations).
- Should we capture time-to-first-meaningful-contribution metric in personnel dashboard?

References and quick links:
- CONFLUENCE-1234 (succession policy draft)
- JIRA-HR-789 (recruitment plan epic)
- github.com/redwood/handbook/pull/56 (handoff ledger template PR)

Retrospective prompts (end of month 3):
- What knowledge gaps persisted longer than expected? Why?
- Which handoff artifacts were most useful? Which were not used?
- What would we change about the 90-day mini-sprint next time?

Notes: keep this doc intentionally concise and action-oriented. People Ops should own templating and enable managers to run the sprint with minimal overhead. This is a living working-playbook — move items to the canonical handbook after 1 successful run.

Quick owner action items (first 72 hours):
- Create handoff ledger and share with stakeholders.
- Block 4x1-hour shadow sessions on calendar.
- Confirm mentor assignment and send welcome note.
- If external hire needed, trigger JIRA-HR-789 and link this ledger.

-- end working draft --
